blocks.content: Where Article 31C comes in, Article 14 goes out.

rows: All individuals are subject to the ordinary law of the land.
President and Governors are exempt from court proceedings under Article 361.
Foreign nationals are subject to local judicial jurisdiction.
Foreign ambassadors and diplomats enjoy diplomatic immunity from local courts.
Fundamental Rights generally supersede Directive Principles.
Laws implementing Art 39(b) & (c) override Art 14 and Art 19 via Article 31C.

items: Questions frequently test whether President or Governor criminal immunity applies to personal acts done prior to entering office.
Remember that Article 31C immunity applies strictly to laws enacted to implement Directive Principles specified in Article 39(b) and 39(c).
Civil proceedings against the President or Governor during their term require a mandatory two-month prior written notice.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 361 provides constitutional immunity to the President and Governors from criminal proceedings during their term of office.
Foreign sovereigns, ambassadors, and diplomats enjoy immunity from both criminal and civil legal proceedings.
Article 31C creates a major exception to equality by giving precedence to Directive Principles under Article 39(b) and (c) over Fundamental Rights.
Parliamentary privileges under Article 105 protect Members of Parliament from legal actions regarding speech or votes cast in Parliament.
